newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Tung calls for calm over disputed islands.
newsitem.headline: HK's Tung calls for calm over disputed islands.

text.p: Hong Kong's post-colonial leader Tung Chee-hwa on Wednesday urged the territory of 6.4 million to cool their tempers over a group of disputed islands in the East China Sea.

"The (Chinese) central government has already made response to the matter. Hong Kong should cool down, allowing the central government to handle it," Tung told a news conference after returning from Beijing.
Tung will run Hong Kong after Beijing resumes sovereignty over the British colony at midnight on June 30.
The islands, uninhabited rocky outcrops lying between Taiwan and Okinawa and administered by Japan, are called Senkaku by Japan, Diaoyu by China and Tiaoyutai by Taiwan.
A diplomatic row over their ownership was triggered by a visit to the islands on Tuesday by a conservative Japanese parliamentarian.
Emotions are running high in Hong Kong, where activists have staged protests outside the Japanese consulate.
Anti-Japanese activists from Hong Kong and Taiwan are planning to sail to the disputed isles on May 18 to "reclaim" them.
Last September, a Hong Kong activist drowned when he jumped into stormy waters near the islands to press China's claim to them.
